endorsements.quote: For example, companies developing or using AI/ML systems can setup specialized processes and teams to review appeal requests from end users or anyone affected by the AI/ML decisions—similar to customer support but focusing instead on specific AI/ML decisions and not on, say, product repairs or returns.

unlisted_practices: Place human expert review at an appeal stage after the AI/ML decision, rather than having a human validate every AI/ML decision.

Set the standard of review on appeal according to the epistemic advantages of humans versus AI, using deferential review for pure accuracy questions and de novo review for questions of model misspecification or fairness.
Direct appeals involving the same AI/ML algorithm or application to a centralized specialized review team that develops expertise and general principles.
Consolidate multiple appealed cases for collective review so that systematic problems such as bias become visible.
Provide free appeal assistants to help poor or vulnerable populations challenge AI/ML decisions.
Consider giving the appellate body discretion over which appeals to hear, with costs or penalties to deter frivolous appeals.

screen.reason: This is a conceptual viewpoint/framework paper proposing an appeals-based human-in-the-loop governance mechanism for AI in healthcare.
